note: L2-01: Two once-per-life keys that lock the vehicle behind a loud countdown, bail the player out and spend the vehicle; only killing it first stops the blast, or you leave the ring.
L2-02: Both throw the players out hurt and leave the dead hull as hard cover with its own health; cover-wreck says it was written from wreck-bunker and has no source.
L2-03: Both take only the victim's weapon for a few seconds while it keeps moving; shake-off and the controller's death end it.
L2-04: Both turn wrecks into money and both are answered by denying or destroying the wrecks first.
L2-05: Both place a fragile device that supplies allies in a radius, answered by shooting it and splashing the crowd around it.
L2-06: Both are a hidden trap that holds the first enemy to touch it; the answer is to detect it or shoot it unsprung.
L2-08: A flying carrier drops all its riders over a chosen spot without landing; anti-air on the carrier and splash on the arrivals answer both.
L2-10: Both are a short dash during which nothing can hurt the unit, both from Dota 2's Time Walk; the answer is to bait it out and punish the recharge.
L2-11: Two keys that make the unit untouchable while it slips through or away; the answers are to wait it out, silence it before it starts and punish the end.
L2-12: Both teleport the unit back to a fixed friendly point to bank cargo or escape, both from Red Alert 2's Chrono Miner; the answer is to catch it on the way out or at the field.
L2-15: Both tie the card to one teammate's squad, follow it, and keep it steadier and healing faster while attached; the answer is to kill or separate the buffer and splash the group.
L2-16: Both put a strong timed buff on an area at range for a price; the answer is to back off for its seconds and stay out of the area.
L2-18: Both stick a device on an enemy thing that stops it until the device is knocked off; the answer is to repair it off or kill the sapper.
L2-19: Both put the carrier on a key into a static bunker so riders can fire; the answers are to catch it moving, flank it and out-range the riders.
L2-21: Both lie buried on a route and fire automatically on the first enemy near; the answers are detection, scans and avoiding the obvious paths.
L2-22: Both bury the card on a route and strike the first enemy that comes near; the answers are a detector, and shooting it when it shows itself.
L2-23: Both plant one or two hidden traps that slow the first enemy over them and ping the owner; the answers are to detect, sweep or take another route.
L2-25: Both turn an enemy turret or device to your side after a warned hack; the answers are to interrupt the hack, kill the hacker and retake it.
L2-26: Both bring teammates out at your position on a key; the answers are to punish the arrivals and kill the caller.
L2-27: The scout drone widens sight, reveals stealthed units or marks enemies over a chosen spot for the team: reveal-area delivered by a drone, and delivery is a variant under the Granularity rule.
L2-28: Both throw a device that hides allies in an area for several seconds; the answers are to walk in, fire area weapons blind or wait it out.

L2-29: worker-crew's own text says lost workers come back as in reinforce-squad's respawning-followers, so a card with both writes the same respawn twice; the answers are to kill the soft followers, then the master.
L2-30: disguised-bomb is a self-destruct carrier that already looks like an ordinary vehicle; copy-target adds a key to choose whose look.
L2-32: Both lay explosives to trap a route and blow them by hand when the right target comes.
L2-33: Both are planted by hand and run a long countdown the enemy can see; only reaching and disarming them in time stops them, so the planter's team guards them.
L2-34: Both are a deploy key that unfolds the vehicle into a team building; the answers are to catch it on the way and then hit the building.
L2-35: modular-bay is exclusive-bay with the passenger bunker picked, riders firing out of it; both cite the Overlord's add-ons.
L3-07: Both are a key for a few seconds of much higher speed; the slump only bites when the boost is overused, a cost lever rather than a second tool.
L3-32: Both put a damaging field on a spot within reach for a few seconds, and the answer is to leave it quickly.
L3-20: Both unfold the vehicle into a stationary, unarmed team building and pack up again; the answers are to catch it unfolded and capture or destroy it.
L3-23: Both pick a spot at range and hurt everyone in the circle after a short, visible warning; the answer is to leave the circle.

X-02: As L2-16, but even closer: minions are spent from a carrier onto a distant spot, so no walk to shoot at; what is left is a buff placed on an area at range for a price, which is placed-blessing..
X-03: Both are the Yuri's Revenge Slave Miner deploying into a refinery that earns for the team and can't move while deployed.
X-04: The twin of L2-28, which the finder named inside L2-28 but did not list: a hiding cover that moves with the unit, one-way darkness versus a two-way smoke cloud.
X-05: The third side of the L2-34 and L3-20 cluster: two deploy keys that turn the vehicle into a team building (one way versus packs up).
